skills.when_to_use: The main question asks whether or where the same particular person or object corresponds across videos, rather than whether objects share a category or appearance. Establish identity candidates from supplied conventions and visible distinguishing evidence, then compare unresolved candidates; do not assume correspondence from video IDs or durations.
skills.strategy: For identity correspondence, extract only the question's supplied target description and label or view conventions; a label in one view does not initialize the same label in another unless the question explicitly establishes that mapping. Use analyze_videos with self-contained local instructions to obtain candidate descriptions, distinguishing features, visible paths, and relevant anchors in each source, asking for missing initialization evidence instead of guessing the target's appearance. Keep all candidates compatible with the supported evidence and retain their source identities in reasoning; category or color similarity alone does not establish the same physical entity. If joint comparison can resolve a distinguishing feature, use watch_videos with an instruction naming the candidates and feature, at least two distinct video_id values, and one in-duration clip per video with start before end and no fps field, using known anchors or first locating the relevant moments. Eliminate a candidate only using an actual incompatible observation or an explicit convention, and leave occlusion or an unobserved feature unresolved rather than converting it into a mismatch. Answer once supported identity evidence resolves the requested correspondence; if ambiguity survives the runtime limit, give the best supported answer in the required format and state the identity limitation in reason without inventing a match.
